title: Value of a client_secret field in an Asana token request
summary: A synthetic value of client_secret beside client_id in a raw form-encoded request to the token endpoint, a curl --data-urlencode argument and a JSON body.
rationale: The field is the carrier: Asana documents the client secret as the client_secret parameter of a form-encoded POST body to the token exchange endpoint, sent from the app server and never exposed to the browser. Asana states no prefix, alphabet or length for the secret, so the value is flagged because of the field it sits in, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only: the field name, the equals sign or colon, the ampersand and the quotes are outside it, and the client_id beside it identifies the application. An HMAC signature in x-asana-request-signature is a derived output, not the secret.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the client_secret field of a token request is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Asana documents the client_secret request parameter at the token exchange endpoint (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The client secret belonging to the app, found in the Basic information tab of the developer console
The browser should not see your client_secret

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
